moves.why: small for +2; 2p changes the math - now sealing opponent's floor denies only +1 vs my +1, so floors dominate

in 2-player, the equilibrium is small-mirror: I claim 3 floors (6pts) then seat 0 and I each seal 3 shelves (3pts) for a 9-9 tie. Any deviation (like playing large) only makes things worse for both of us. Small on bore 1 mirrors seat 0's small on bore 0
small on empty bore for +2; at 2p optimal play is "claim all floors, seal own floors" - tie at 9-9 unless someone deviates

still in the small-mirror phase. I have 1 small left; seat 0 just took their 2nd floor (they had 2 smalls, now 1). Mirroring on bore 3 means I take my last floor and we each have 3 floors (6pts each) before shelves. Any other play either loses a floor or burns a large before the small-mirror completes
small for +2; math at 2p: 3 smalls then seal own two floors = 3*2 + 2*1 = 8 each, tie. Sealing opponent's floor here is -1 net for me

take the last empty floor — denies seat 0 a 4th floor (they're at 3, I'd reach 3 too at 6pts each, instead of seat 0 hitting 8pts). After this we both have 3 floors + 3 shelves available; seat 0 goes next with 1 small remaining, will play it on... wait, no floors left empty. Seat 0's small has nowhere to go (all floors filled). So seat 0 must now play large. I can seal my floors next round with my 3 larges

both smalls gone; now must seal. At 2p sealing OWN floor is +1 (opponent loses nothing), sealing OPPONENT'S is +1 but opponent loses nothing since no more floors to claim. All options are +1 regardless of choice

all 5 unsealed bores will be sealed (no smalls left, no floors empty), and I'll take 3 of those 5 seals while seat 0 takes 2 — final result 9-9 tie regardless of which bore I pick. Picking bore 1 (leftmost open)
seal own floor for +1; same outcome regardless of bore
final sealing. Total shelves I'll end with = 3, seat 0 ends with 3. Both score 9. Any bore is identical here
only legal move. Seals bore 5, taking my 3rd shelf. Final: 9-9 tie
